items.title: [partial] Diffusion Policy Push-T (state, CNN) reports 0.946 max test mean score
items.content_text: An independent re-implementation in LeRobot (lerobot/diffusion_pusht) trained Diffusion Policy on Push-T and measured 0.955 average max overlap and a 65.4% success rate (episodes reaching 95% overlap) over 500 evaluation episodes, against the authors' reported 0.946 max test mean score. A model trained with the original Diffusion Policy code and evaluated in the same LeRobot harness scored 0.957 average max overlap and 64.2% success, so the port matches the original implementation within about a point on both metrics. Limits: the paper's number is the best evaluation over training (max key over 3 runs), while the LeRobot numbers come from a single seed at a fixed 175k-step checkpoint; the 95%-overlap success rate has no direct counterpart in the paper's Push-T table; the training data is LeRobot's own conversion of the Push-T demonstrations. The paper's real-robot Push-T results are untested here.

items.title: [partial] ACT reaches 50% on sim Cube Transfer and 20% on sim Bimanual Insertion with human demonstrations
items.content_text: Third-party runs of ACT in the LeRobot port land in a similar range but are not like-for-like. The LeRobot team's model card reports 83.0% on Transfer Cube over 500 episodes for its own re-implementation, and 68.0% for weights trained with the original ACT repo and evaluated in LeRobot. It says the code was heavily refactored and that its environment may score success differently (success can register on the second gripper's contact with the cube), so those figures are not directly comparable to the paper's 50%. Later users report lower numbers with the current LeRobot code: about 50-60% over 500 episodes on Transfer Cube (issue #2605, which also cites 8% on Insertion against the 20% LeRobot reports), and 66% over 50 episodes in a separate run (issue #4168). One comment in #2605 reports 34% on a custom Isaac task against 90% with the original ACT code, which is a different environment. None of these is a 3-seed, 50-evaluation rerun in the paper's own environment, so seeds, evaluation counts, environment port and success definition all differ. The evidence supports the claim loosely on Transfer Cube and is mixed on Insertion. It does not show the paper's numbers are wrong.

items.title: [untested] Octo out of the box averages 29% higher success than RT-1-X across three robot setups
items.content_text: No independent reproduction of this exact three-setup comparison was found. The nearest follow-up is SIMPLER (arXiv:2405.05941), a paired sim-and-real evaluation benchmark, but it shares authors with Octo (Pertsch, Mees, Walke, Levine, Finn, Vuong, Xiao appear on both papers) and evaluates different tasks, so it is not an independent rerun. The real numbers it aggregates for four BridgeV2 WidowX tasks (Octo-Base 33.3% / 25.0% / 0% / 25.0% vs RT-1-X 0% on all four) re-cite the original teams' own evaluations, and its simulated scores for the released Octo checkpoints fall far below the real numbers (e.g. Google robot move-near 4.2% sim vs 35.0% real), a real-to-sim gap the SIMPLER authors document. Independent attempts adjacent to the claim: one user's pre-training rerun at batch 128 vs 2048 reported much worse SIMPLER scores (issue #151, unanswered); another user's custom-sim fine-tune got 60% success with language goals but 0% with image goals, while the paper reports goal images ahead of language by 25% on WidowX tasks (issue #157, custom environment). Neither re-runs the paper's real-robot protocol.

items.title: [replicated] LeRobot reproduces Pi0.5 LIBERO results (97.5% average)
items.content_text: One outside evaluator first measured 71.75% average with a non-documented setup. After setting policy.n_action_steps=10 as the docs specify, they reported 96.75% average against the documented 97.5%, a near match from a single run with 10 episodes per task. One evaluator on the same LeRobot harness is limited evidence: it does not show the result holds across seeds, simulators or hardware. The n_action_steps setting changes results a lot, so check it when comparing numbers.

items.title: [not reproduced] LeRobot Pi0 LIBERO checkpoint matches reported success rates
items.content_text: Observation 1 (four suites, issue #2114): an outside user measured 64.75% average (Spatial 69, Object 72, Goal 83, Long 35) and, after changing MuJoCo version and seed, 71%, which they described as 10 to 20 points under the figures they were comparing to. A LeRobot maintainer replied that the Pi0 checkpoint needs more training to reach paper-level results. Observation 2 (LIBERO-Goal only, issue #2156, a different user): about 75% with n_action_steps=50 and about 90% with n_action_steps=10 for the same checkpoint. This is one suite, so it says nothing about the other three. Together: results for this checkpoint depend strongly on evaluation settings, and the reference target is not pinned here, so this ledger cannot say how large the gap is. 'Not reproduced' reflects a third-party attempt that did not match what the reporter expected, not that anything was misreported. Checkpoint versions may also have changed since (the model card now names a v044 variant).

items.title: [partial] OpenVLA-OFT reaches 97.1% average success on LIBERO
items.content_text: Mixed, with a setup explanation. A third-party LeRobot port evaluated the released checkpoints and reported 96.85% average over 500 episodes per suite against 97.1% in the paper (before a precision fix the port's author notes). In issue #150, one user ran 50 episodes per task with seed 7 on an RTX 4090 and got 95.8% average, with Spatial at 93.2% against 97.6%; another commenter reported reaching about 99% on Spatial after reinstalling with mujoco==3.3.2. In issue #128, users evaluating the released checkpoints reported much lower Spatial results (56.6% and 58.0%) and the thread discusses the MuJoCo version, which one commenter says changes floor rendering. This ledger did not read the thread through to a confirmed resolution. Taken together: the headline is approached by some independent runs and missed badly by others, and results appear sensitive to the simulator version. All figures here come from user reports and a port's README, not controlled replications.

items.title: [partial] OpenVLA fine-tuned reaches 76.5% average success on LIBERO
items.content_text: Third-party runs land close on some suites and far off on others. One user's single-trial run averaged 73.75% (Goal 74.2, Long 48.4). A separate single-seed, 100-rollout-per-suite run using the official checkpoints averaged 67.0%, with Object at 60.0% against 88.4% reported, while Long (53.0%) and Goal (77.0%) were near the reported numbers. Neither run is a full 3-seed, 50-episode replication, so differences may be noise, hardware or rendering. Not enough to call the claim wrong.
